scenes.narration: Costco sold almost 300 billion dollars of stuff last year. So why does it barely make money selling it?
Costco keeps its prices barely above cost, so the store itself runs on razor thin margins.
The real engine is the membership card. Last year, membership fees brought in 5.9 billion dollars, compared with 9.2 billion in total profit.
It's why the hot dog and soda still cost a dollar fifty, the same price since 1985. Cheap deals keep you renewing.
With over 80 million paid members, Costco gets paid before you even grab a cart.
So Costco isn't really a store. It's a membership club that happens to sell groceries.
